streamlabs-chat-overlay.title: Custom chat overlay in Streamlabs Desktop: setup & examples
streamlabs-chat-overlay.description: Add a ChatStyle chat design to Streamlabs Desktop with a Browser Source. Keep your existing scenes and compare Small Talk, Lofi Windows 93 and Neo Tokyo.
streamlabs-chat-overlay.heading: Your own chat in Streamlabs.
streamlabs-chat-overlay.intro: Already using Streamlabs Desktop? You can keep your scene layout and add a separately styled chat through a Browser Source. The important distinction is between the broadcasting app and the service that supplies the chat design.
streamlabs-chat-overlay.answer: Use the configured ChatStyle overlay URL in a Browser Source. The built-in Streamlabs Chat Box and a ChatStyle template are separate widgets; pasting a template shop link into the native Chat Box does not convert it.
steps: Prepare one replacement
Keep your current chat source while setting up the new one. Choose a template below, configure it in ChatStyle and copy the live overlay URL provided for your channel.
Create a Browser Source
In Streamlabs Desktop, use Sources → + → Browser Source. Give it a recognizable name such as ChatStyle chat, then paste the overlay URL.
Match the reserved space
Set the source width and height for your chat area. Try a long message before resizing the source in the scene; squeezed text and clipped frames need different fixes.
Check for duplicate chat
Send a new message and inspect the scene. Once the new chat works, hide the old chat source. Switch scenes once and confirm that only the intended widget is visible.

examples.why: A compact option for an existing scene with a narrow chat area. Check whether the longest username still fits after replacing your previous widget.
A distinctive desktop-window alternative. Leave space around the title bars rather than cropping it to the outline of an old, plain chat box.
A stronger terminal look for a dark scene. Compare its animation with your existing alerts before adding more movement.

notes: Two different settings panels
Template appearance belongs in ChatStyle; placement belongs in Streamlabs Desktop. Change one side at a time so you can see what caused the result.
Keep a fallback
Do a short recording before removing the old source. A working preview of a template is not yet proof that your channel's live messages are connected.
faq: Do I need to rebuild my scene collection?
No. Add the new browser source to your existing scene, test it, then hide the widget it replaces.
Can I paste the ChatStyle design into Streamlabs Custom CSS?
That is not the workflow here. Use ChatStyle's configured overlay URL as its own Browser Source.

obs-chat-not-showing.title: Chat overlay not showing in OBS? Check the source step by step
obs-chat-not-showing.description: Find why a chat overlay is blank, hidden or cut off in OBS. Follow a short diagnostic path before testing Small Talk, Inline Flow or Sleeping Cats.
obs-chat-not-showing.heading: Chat not showing in OBS?
obs-chat-not-showing.intro: A blank chat does not automatically mean the design is broken. First find out whether messages reach the overlay at all, then check what OBS is displaying. Keep your current template while diagnosing the problem.
obs-chat-not-showing.answer: Send a fresh message, check the configured overlay URL, then inspect visibility and source order. If the overlay works in a browser but not in OBS, focus on the source settings rather than changing templates.

reference.title: Start with what you see
rows: No messages anywhere
Correct channel, live connection and a fresh test message.
Works in browser, blank in OBS
Exact URL, visible source and source order.
Only part of the bubble appears
Browser viewport dimensions and cropping.
Disappears after switching scenes
Visibility and browser refresh/shutdown settings.

steps: Separate connection from layout
Open your configured overlay in a browser and send a new chat message. If nothing arrives there either, confirm the channel and connection in the provider dashboard first.
Inspect the OBS scene
Make sure the browser source is visible and sits above any opaque background or gameplay source that could cover it. Confirm you are looking at the scene being output.
Check the source rectangle
Inspect width, height and any crop in Edit Transform. A very narrow viewport can wrap every word; an accidental crop can hide the message area entirely.
Refresh once, then retest
After correcting the URL or settings, refresh the browser source and send another message. Repeatedly refreshing an idle chat makes it harder to tell whether new content is arriving.

examples.why: Its compact shape is useful when checking whether a narrow scene slot is the cause of clipping. Use the live channel configuration for the actual test.
A restrained layout makes it easier to inspect text width against the available space. It is a design comparison, not a repair for a disconnected source.
The cats make top-edge cropping easy to spot. If they disappear while the bubble remains, inspect the crop and reserved height.

notes: OBS dock versus broadcast
A chat dock you read inside OBS is not necessarily a source visible to viewers. Check the actual scene preview or a short recording.
Record the failing case
Note whether it fails on first load, after a scene change or only with long messages. That distinction is more useful than changing several settings together.
faq: Will a different template fix an empty chat?
Not if the overlay is connected to the wrong channel or its source is hidden. Diagnose the connection and scene first.
Why did the old messages disappear?
A refreshed browser source may rebuild its view. Test with a fresh message instead of assuming that previous conversation history must be restored.

transparent-chat-overlay.title: Transparent Twitch chat overlay in OBS: background & bubble guide
transparent-chat-overlay.description: Remove an unwanted page background while keeping chat bubbles readable. Compare Inline Flow, Small Talk and Violet Frame Slim with practical OBS checks.
transparent-chat-overlay.heading: A transparent chat overlay for OBS.
transparent-chat-overlay.intro: A transparent chat overlay can still have colored message bubbles. Think of the empty space around the messages and the fill inside each bubble as two separate layers.
transparent-chat-overlay.answer: Place the chat above a colored test background in OBS. If a full rectangle hides that background, inspect the overlay page; if only individual bubbles have a fill, that may be part of the intended design.
steps: Use the live overlay
Load the URL for your configured chat. A shop page, gallery image or preview video can include a backdrop and should not be used as the live source.
Add a contrast test
Temporarily place a bright color source behind the chat. Look between messages and around corners to identify which area is actually opaque.
Inspect background settings
Check the provider's appearance settings and any Custom CSS you added. OBS's default Browser Source CSS makes the page body transparent; it does not erase every nested panel or image.
Keep enough contrast
Test the final chat over a bright and a dark scene. If transparent text disappears, choose a bubble with its own readable surface or reserve a quiet part of the scene.

examples.why: Compare this slim design when you want more of the scene to remain visible. Judge the letters against moving content, not just a still background.
Small bubbles provide a compromise between a clear message area and a compact footprint. Leave room for messages that wrap onto another line.
A narrow framed direction when plain text feels too exposed. Check the frame's visibility in both light and dark moments.

notes: Avoid a universal CSS fix
Selectors differ between widgets. Removing every background can also remove the bubble fill that makes the text readable.
Preview backdrops
The colored backgrounds in our template videos help show the designs. Check transparency in your configured live overlay inside OBS.
faq: Should I use chroma key on a black chat background?
First identify where the background comes from. Keying out a color can also remove matching details in the chat; native transparency is a better starting point.
Does transparent mean no message background?
No. A transparent page can contain opaque message bubbles, outlines and decorative elements.

free-twitch-chat-overlays.title: Free Twitch chat overlays: two real ChatStyle templates
free-twitch-chat-overlays.description: Compare Zuluxxman and Manhunt 2026, two JesusTenG chat templates listed as free on ChatStyle. Preview their designs and follow a practical first-stream checklist.
free-twitch-chat-overlays.heading: Free chat overlays for Twitch.
free-twitch-chat-overlays.intro: A first stream does not need an elaborate overlay pack. These two JesusTenG templates were listed as free on ChatStyle when checked on 11 November 2026. Both have an individual preview and a direct template link below.
free-twitch-chat-overlays.answer: Choose Zuluxxman for a turquoise HUD direction or Manhunt 2026 for a darker orange-accented look. The free label refers to the template listing; check ChatStyle for current account options and any separate service costs.
steps: Choose by fit, not price alone
Compare the design against your normal scene. If neither matches, keep a simple temporary layout rather than adding colors that clash with everything else.
Check the original listing
Open the template on ChatStyle and confirm its current Free label and available options. This page does not promise that every ChatStyle feature is free.
Try a restrained variant
Explore the listed skins in the detail view. Start with one consistent look before introducing several different colors for your viewers.
Make a short test recording
Configure the overlay, add its URL to your broadcasting software and test real messages. Check names, wrapping and contrast at the final stream size.

examples.why: Turquoise accents and a broadcast-HUD feel. A good comparison for cool-colored scenes; check how its frame stands out over bright gameplay.
A dark tactical design with orange highlights. Try it when your existing layout already uses warm accents and gives event effects enough room.

notes: A chat template, not a complete pack
These examples style the conversation. They do not supply your webcam frame, starting screen, microphone setup or streaming account.
Current terms live on ChatStyle
Prices and access can change. The original template page is the place to confirm availability before configuring your channel.
faq: Are all templates in this gallery free?
No. This guide deliberately selects the two templates marked free in our current catalog. Other designs may have a template price.
Is there a free download button here?
These are browser-based chat templates configured on ChatStyle. Use the original template link to get started; the gallery video is only a preview.

youtube-chat-overlay-obs.title: YouTube live chat overlay in OBS: channel, source & design
youtube-chat-overlay-obs.description: Plan a YouTube live chat overlay with ChatStyle: check the connected channel, active broadcast and OBS source, then compare three readable chat designs.
youtube-chat-overlay-obs.heading: YouTube chat in your OBS scene.
youtube-chat-overlay-obs.intro: For a YouTube stream, start with the right channel and broadcast before choosing the frame. ChatStyle documents YouTube support and read-only channel access; the overlay still needs a live conversation to display.
youtube-chat-overlay-obs.answer: Connect the intended YouTube or Brand channel in ChatStyle, configure the chat there and use its overlay URL in OBS. A YouTube watch-page URL and a configured chat-overlay URL serve different purposes.
steps: Check the YouTube conversation
Open your intended broadcast in YouTube Studio and verify that live chat is available. Chat is unavailable on content set as made for kids; an overlay cannot restore a disabled chat.
Confirm the channel connection
Use ChatStyle's Google/YouTube connection flow and verify the selected channel. If you manage several channels, compare the name with the broadcast you intend to stream.
Configure a chat design
Choose a template below and complete the overlay setup in ChatStyle. Confirm that a new message from the intended broadcast arrives before adjusting its appearance.
Place and test the OBS source
Add the configured overlay URL as a Browser Source. Send a message with a long channel name, record a short sample and check it at phone size.

examples.why: A compact choice for a tutorial or demonstration where most of the screen belongs to the content. Test long channel names in the available width.
A softer botanical frame for a relaxed conversation. Reserve a dedicated area so its decoration does not compete with on-screen instructions.
A desktop-inspired direction for a creative or retro scene. Keep the window details large enough to survive a small video player.

notes: Check the next broadcast too
Before each stream, confirm that the connection is showing the intended live conversation. A successful test with one broadcast is not a check of another.
Keep platform features separate
This guide covers displaying chat. Check current ChatStyle options for platform-specific events and access controls rather than assuming Twitch features are identical on YouTube.
faq: Does this change YouTube's own chat panel?
The template styles the chat displayed inside your stream video. YouTube controls its native chat interface.
Can ChatStyle edit my YouTube videos?
Its published permissions describe read-only YouTube access, without video upload, edit or delete permissions. Review the current permissions page when connecting.

animated-chat-overlays.title: Animated Twitch chat overlays: compare motion before you choose
animated-chat-overlays.description: Compare Neo Tokyo, Magical Love and Manhunt 2026 in motion. Choose an animated chat overlay by message arrival, reading time and fit with your scene.
animated-chat-overlays.heading: Chat overlays in motion.
animated-chat-overlays.intro: An animated chat overlay should make a new message noticeable while leaving time to read it. Compare the whole sequence: arrival, resting state and what happens when several messages arrive close together.
animated-chat-overlays.answer: Watch each original video, then test your chosen overlay alongside the actual game and alerts. A dramatic solo preview and a comfortable full stream are different viewing situations.
steps: Watch one full message cycle
Open each detail page and look beyond the first frame. Notice when the username becomes readable, when the message settles and whether an effect keeps moving afterward.
Compare quiet and busy chat
Test a few messages separated by pauses, then a short burst. If several entrances overlap visually, simplify other moving elements around the chat.
Leave a resting area
Put the chat where text stays readable after the effect ends. Avoid positioning it directly over subtitles, rapidly changing menus or another animated widget.
Record under normal load
Test with your normal game, camera and alerts running. Compare recordings and OBS performance before and after adding the overlay; a video preview is not a performance benchmark.

examples.why: A terminal-inspired presentation with a noticeable message reveal. Watch when the real message becomes legible, especially during a burst of conversation.
A playful alternative for a brighter scene. Compare the timing of its details with your alert animations so both are not demanding attention at once.
A darker, cinematic direction with prominent event styling. Try ordinary messages and supported events separately when configuring the live overlay.

notes: A calmer surrounding scene
You can retain an expressive chat by simplifying nearby borders, widgets and moving backgrounds. Animation does not need to occupy every area.
No universal FPS promise
Performance depends on your setup and configuration. Test the real browser source; the gallery plays a video demonstration.
faq: Do I add the preview video as a media source?
No. The video demonstrates the design. Live messages come from the configured ChatStyle overlay URL.
Can I stop the gallery animation?
Use the pause control on the hero or detail preview. The gallery also respects reduced-motion preferences; live overlay settings are managed separately.

just-chatting-overlay.title: Just Chatting overlay layout: camera, chat & three design ideas
just-chatting-overlay.description: Build a Just Chatting scene around your camera and conversation. Compare Sleeping Cats, WhatsChat LoFi and Chat Garden with a practical layout plan.
just-chatting-overlay.heading: Build your Just Chatting scene.
just-chatting-overlay.intro: A Just Chatting scene gives the conversation more space than a gameplay scene. Begin with the relationship between your camera and chat, then choose a design that fills the reserved area comfortably.
just-chatting-overlay.answer: For a first layout, place a large camera area beside a dedicated chat column. Treat that as a sketch: the final balance depends on your framing, message length and whether you also share a browser or guest.
steps: Frame the camera first
Choose the face and upper-body framing you want viewers to see. Leave room for gestures and avoid putting messages across your face or lower-third labels.
Reserve a chat column
Start with roughly a quarter to a third of the scene for chat, then adjust after testing. Keep a visible gap between the camera edge and decorative bubbles.
Introduce the template
Compare the three examples in that same space. A familiar messenger frame, a botanical bubble and decorative cats create different moods without requiring more widgets.
Rehearse a shared-screen moment
If you sometimes show a website or guest, switch to that layout and check where chat goes. Do not let the conversation cover the content you are discussing.

examples.why: The cats work well as a visible motif beside the camera. Leave room above the first message instead of placing it flush against a panel edge.
A messenger-like direction that gives a conversation its own recognizable window. Compare its overall footprint with your planned chat column.
A botanical alternative when you want softer decoration around the conversation. Repeat one of its colors in the rest of the scene.

notes: Avoid empty-screen decoration
If chat is quiet, the camera should still carry the composition. Add only information that helps viewers understand the current segment.
These are chat designs
The examples do not include a complete Just Chatting scene pack. You arrange the camera and other sources in your streaming software.
faq: How wide should the chat be?
There is no universal width. Test a long name and a multiline message inside your proposed column before choosing the final camera-to-chat ratio.
Should I use the same layout for gaming?
You can reuse the design while changing its placement. A game with important HUD elements usually needs a different balance.

vertical-chat-overlay.title: Vertical chat overlay layout: plan a readable 9:16 stream
vertical-chat-overlay.description: Arrange chat in a vertical stream without covering the subject. Use a 1080 × 1920 layout sketch and compare Small Talk, Inline Flow and Violet Frame Slim.
vertical-chat-overlay.heading: Your chat overlay in 9:16.
vertical-chat-overlay.intro: A vertical scene has less horizontal room for names and messages. Build a separate composition for it instead of squeezing a complete landscape scene into a tall frame.
vertical-chat-overlay.answer: Use a 9:16 layout such as 1080 × 1920 as a starting canvas. Reserve a defined chat area, then test on the actual destination's phone interface. Canvas shape does not determine which chat platforms a provider supports.

reference.title: A starting layout sketch
rows: Main subject
Camera or game action with room around faces and key HUD elements.
Chat zone
A short, readable column or band with enough width for a multiline message.
Interface edges
Spare space for the destination app's buttons and captions; verify on a phone.

steps: Choose the focal area
Place the subject before adding chat. Decide whether the most important action is a face, a game character or a demonstration, and keep that region clear.
Give text its own space
Try chat below or beside the focal area. Increase the text area's width if every few words wrap; shrinking the entire overlay makes the letters smaller too.
Check several message shapes
Test one short message, a long username and a multiline message. Keep decoration inside the reserved zone even when several bubbles are visible.
Review the destination view
Watch a test at phone size with the platform interface visible. Move chat away from buttons or captions that overlap it, then check again after changing orientation or player size.

examples.why: A useful compact starting point for a small reserved chat zone. Test that its bubble width still leaves enough room for normal messages.
A restrained direction when the subject needs most of the frame. Use a quiet backdrop so reducing decoration does not reduce legibility.
A slim framed option for separating chat from the main image. Check its full outline near the destination app's interface edges.

notes: No universal safe-area numbers
Player interfaces vary. The layout sketch is a design starting point, not a guaranteed safe area for every platform or device.
Platform support is separate
This guide covers composition. It does not promise that ChatStyle reads TikTok or Kick chat; confirm the supported connection before planning a live feed.
faq: Can I just crop my horizontal scene?
You can test a crop, but it may remove the chat or shrink the subject. A separate vertical composition gives you control over both.
Does 9:16 make every chat provider compatible?
No. Aspect ratio describes the picture. The provider still needs a supported connection to the chat you want to display.

obs-stream-scenes.title: OBS stream scenes for beginners: gameplay, chatting & breaks
obs-stream-scenes.description: Plan a small OBS scene collection and decide where chat belongs. Compare Inline Flow, Sleeping Cats and Lofi Windows 93 for gameplay, conversation and breaks.
obs-stream-scenes.heading: Your first OBS scenes.
obs-stream-scenes.intro: Start with a few scenes you will actually use. Decide what viewers should focus on during gameplay, a conversation or a break, and give chat a deliberate place in each.
obs-stream-scenes.answer: A practical first collection can contain Gameplay, Just Chatting and Break. Add a Starting Soon scene only if you need it. You do not need a new chat design for every scene; consistent styling can connect them.

reference.title: A small scene plan
rows: Gameplay
Secondary to the game; keep it away from HUD and subtitles.
Just Chatting
Part of the main conversation beside a larger camera view.
Break
Optional conversation area beside a clear break message.
Starting Soon
Optional; do not imply a start time you will not keep.

steps: Name scenes by purpose
Create only the scene states you expect to switch between. Clear names such as Gameplay and Break make live operation easier than several nearly identical layout names.
Place the essential sources
Arrange the game or camera before decorative elements. Add the configured chat where it supports that scene's purpose; it does not have to appear everywhere.
Keep one visual thread
Reuse a template or a small color palette across the collection. If you change the chat's footprint, retest long messages instead of assuming the old layout still fits.
Rehearse a complete switch
Record yourself going from gameplay to conversation to break and back. Check chat visibility, accidental duplicate messages, camera framing and sound at every transition.

examples.why: A restrained gameplay candidate where the game should dominate. Place it in a genuinely quiet region rather than covering important interface elements.
An expressive option for a conversation-led scene. Its recognizable motif can also carry across a calmer break layout.
A consistent desktop theme that can tie several scenes together. Keep the chat window readable even when its position changes.

notes: Collection versus output settings
OBS scene collections contain scenes and sources. Output settings belong to profiles; changing the collection is not a substitute for checking the streaming profile.
Check a break privately first
Make sure the break scene hides anything you do not intend to broadcast. A decorative break message does not automatically hide other sources.
faq: Do I need four different templates?
No. Start with one design that suits the channel and adapt its placement. The examples show different approaches, not a required shopping list.
Is this a downloadable OBS scene collection?
No. It is a layout plan with chat-template examples. Create and arrange the sources in your own OBS collection.

viewer-chat-bubbles.title: Custom Twitch chat bubbles for viewers: skins & channel access
viewer-chat-bubbles.description: Plan viewer-selectable Twitch chat skins with ChatStyle. Compare three exact variants, set a clear visual range and test the viewer experience.
viewer-chat-bubbles.heading: Custom chat bubbles for your viewers.
viewer-chat-bubbles.intro: Viewer skins are useful when you want individual messages to have their own look while the channel still feels consistent. Start with a small, intentional selection rather than every possible variant.
viewer-chat-bubbles.answer: The streamer controls skin availability in ChatStyle. Viewers sign in, visit the channel's shop and choose a skin they can access. The result appears in the stream overlay, not as a theme for Twitch's native chat panel.
steps: Set a visual boundary
Choose one template and compare a light, dark and accent variant where available. Keep similar text contrast across the options so a personal color choice does not make a message harder to read.
Decide who should see each option
Use the available channel controls to define access. Write down the intended experience for a new viewer and a regular before adding many role-specific choices.
Test from the viewer side
Ask a willing tester to select an available skin and send a message. Check the actual overlay result; a selection in this gallery is only a preview and does not update a live viewer account.
Introduce a short selection
Show viewers where to choose and explain any access limits clearly. Expand the selection after seeing whether people can find and use the first options without confusion.

examples.why: Candy demonstrates a soft pink-and-purple direction. Compare it with other Sleeping Cats variants when defining a coherent range for one channel.
Lavender keeps the desktop-window identity while changing the palette. Use it as a reference for how much variation your scene can comfortably support.
Blue provides a darker terminal example. Test the message and username contrast before introducing similarly dark choices to viewers.

notes: Preview selection is local
Choosing a skin here updates the gallery link. Activation, viewer eligibility and channel configuration happen on ChatStyle.
Different roles, clear expectations
Avoid promising that everyone can use every skin. Explain the availability you actually configured for your channel.
faq: Can viewers change the whole stream layout?
This workflow concerns their message appearance within the options the streamer makes available. Camera placement and scene layout remain separate.
Why can someone see a preview but not select it live?
A public preview does not establish access in a particular channel. Check that channel's configured skin availability on ChatStyle.
